stories.title: Spain sees record 5,232 heat-related deaths this summer
stories.summary: The overwhelming majority of those who died from the effects of heat this summer were people over the age of 65
article_sentences: MADRID, August 31.
The number of deaths linked to extremely hot weather in Spain during the summer period has reached an all-time high, with 5,232 people dead.
According to data from the daily mortality monitoring system, 2,147 people died from high temperatures in August alone this year.
The current figures have already exceeded the previous annual highs - 4,789 deaths recorded in 2022 and 3,035 cases in 2023.
The overwhelming majority of those who died from the effects of heat this summer were people over the age of 65, accounting for 5,048 cases.
Spaniards over the age of 85 remain the most vulnerable group.
Spanish meteorologists previously reported that the first half of 2026 was the warmest in the kingdom in the past 65 years.
June this year was the second-warmest June on record, while July was the hottest and driest since records began in 1961.

stories.title: Korean police under fire after backtracking on hanging evidence in missing woman’s death in Jeju
stories.summary: Police initially claimed forensic evidence showed Jang Mi-ran died by hanging, but later said the cause of death could not be determined due to severe decomposition. Family and boyfriend disputed the suicide theory, raising doubts about police conclusions and the physical consistency of the hanging scenario. Police are under scrutiny for mishandling the case, including improper closure of missing person reports by an officer, prompting a review of 298 cases. Police investigating the death of Jang Mi-ran came under fire on Aug 31 after saying they could not determine how the 37-year-old died, despite having repeatedly suggested that forensic evidence indicated hanging. Jang’s body was discovered Aug 24 at a palm tree farm in Hallim-eup, Jeju City, 104 days after she disappeared. Local police said at the time they believed she had hung herself based on the position of the body and had later claimed an autopsy supported that conclusion. But the National Forensic Service, which carried out the autopsy, was unable to establish a cause of death, adding that it was open to other possibilties. “The cause of death could not be determined because the body was severely decomposed,” Hong Sug-gi, head of the National Office of Investigation, said on Aug 31. “We are investigating while keeping all possibilities open.” The change in stance raises further questions about a case already alleged to have been deliberately mishandled. A senior police official later said investigators were primarily considering suicide after examining the scene. Acting National.

stories.title: Japan seeks record $70.9b defence budget, with AI focus
stories.summary: Japan’s defence ministry requested a record budget of 8.9 trillion yen (S$70.9 billion) on Aug 31 as Tokyo looks to artificial intelligence to speed up decision-making in the face of a tense security environment. The final budget reportedly could reach 10 trillion yen as Tokyo undergoes a sweeping upgrade of its defence in order to navigate growing tension with neighbours such as China, North Korea and Russia. The latest request focuses on countering “new ways of warfare”, with an emphasis on the use of AI, drones and standoff missiles. Under the request, the ministry hopes to implement an AI-powered decision support system. It also wants to procure low-cost drones that can work in tandem with long-range missiles to neutralise enemy assets. The ministry said it plans to develop underwater-launched hypersonic missiles and establish a new unit to bolster defences against cognitive warfare, a growing threat aimed at shaping public opinion through disinformation campaigns and other operations. The budget request for the fiscal year starting from April 2027 highlights the latest step by Japan to boost its military to meet the volatile geopolitical reality, gradually shedding its traditional pacifist stance that limited the use of force purely for self-defence. China’s rapid military expansion and North Korea’s steady development of missiles and nuclear weapons have pressed Japan to shore up its defence. Russia’s war in Ukraine has fuelled worries among Japanese policymakers that a similar conflict could erupt in East Asia, considering China’s mounting pressure on Taiwan and its escalating territorial disputes with Japan. The Nikkei newspaper said the defence ministry’s request may jump to more than 10 trillion yen, citing an unnamed ruling party lawmaker. The current request did not specify the estimated costs of many products and services, including missiles, drones and digital systems. These figures will be finalised once the government finishes its revision of core national security documents by the end of the year, defence officials said.

stories.title: US renews attack on Iran while threatening financial sanctions on Tehran allies
stories.summary: Hostilities between the US and Iran resumed after a month's pause. The US said Iran was preparing to launch sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Iran retaliated by hitting US military bases in Jordan. Meanwhile, the US Treasury Secretary said there would be more economic sanctions on the way for banks doing business with Iran.

stories.title: Artificial Intelligence in Europe: does advanced AI have a glass ceiling?
stories.summary: What does Europe lose if advanced AI adoption stays at current levels? A report commissioned by US tech giant Amazon Web Services finds that skills shortages and regulatory uncertainty are hindering AI adoption in Europe and 38% of European startups are looking to move abroad. Charles Pellegrin talks to Sasha Rubel, AWS's head of generative AI policy for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

stories.title: Colombian rebel group say kidnapped French Foreign Legion soldier is still alive
stories.summary: Rebels from the Central General Staff, the main splinter group of Colombia's defunct FARC guerrillas, on Sunday said they were responsible for kidnapping a Colombian national serving in the elite French Foreign Legion. The guerrillas said that Jose Olger Melo Charry, who was reportedly on leave in his home country, was alive and in "perfect health".
